newsitem.title: USA: NYNEX files to offer long distance in NY.
newsitem.headline: NYNEX files to offer long distance in NY.

text.p: NYNEX Corp on Tuesday said it filed with the New York Public Service Commission (NYPSC) a draft application for entry into the long-distance telephone market in New York State.

The draft filing is a preliminary step, and allows a 60 day review period with the commission so that by early April when any modifications needed have been made, NYNEX could meet all requirements to offer long distance, the company said.
The 1996 Telecom Act mandates a 14-point checklist for regional Bells before they can provide long distance in their own local calling markets.
The checklist is a measure of how open to competition NYNEX's local calling markets are.
"Fifty wireline carriers and 23 wireless carriers are certified by the NYPSC to provide competitive local exchange services in New York," said Don Reed, NYNEX President and Group Executive.

A NYNEX spokeswoman said that NYNEX may not meet all the 14 points on the checklist now, but would do by the time the review period was over. NYNEX would also need Federal Communications Commission approval to offer long distance.
Ameritech Corp, the first regional Bell to apply to enter the long distance market in its home territories, gained approval from state regulators in Michigan this month.
However Ameritech withdrew its application at the FCC stage after a dispute over documentation. (( Nick Louth, New York Newsroom 212 859 1712))
